The grant of "access to, and the right to use" HDI's hosting system and administration tools is limited to "the Company" alone: it names neither our affiliates nor contractors acting on our behalf, and gives no mechanism (e.g. written notice) to add them, so it fails even the fallback position. Section 10.3 (Assignment) binds successors and assigns, so successor transfer is largely covered, but affiliate/contractor scope is not. We propose a short subsection extending the rights to affiliates and contractors, confirming they are not revocable at HDI's discretion (only for uncured material breach or on termination), and confirming successor transferability; affiliate coverage on prior written notice is offered as a fallback.

quote: 6.1 Except as provided in Section 6.2, during the term of this Agreement, the Company shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products (including, without limitation, the products of Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled and companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled) and HDI shall have the exclusive right to use of the "Deerskin" brand for a self-contained web site for the offering of Deerskin Products directly to the consumer on the Internet.
rationale: Section 6.1 does impose a field-of-use restriction on the Company (our client), so the preferred position (no restriction at all) is not met. However, it sits squarely at the playbook fallback and should not be redlined. (1) Scope is limited to a named product set: the defined term "Deerskin Products" (which expressly excludes closeout merchandise and the Joan Cook Catalog per §1.1) plus named comparators Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled — this is not an undefined "any competing business." (2) It is further confined to a single medium and format — "any project similar to the Site on the Internet" — leaving the Company's catalog, wholesale and bricks-and-mortar channels wholly unrestricted. (3) It runs "during the term of this Agreement" only, with no post-term tail, and the term under §4.1 is a one-year period auto-renewing annually and terminable by either Party on 90 days' notice, so the restraint is effectively capped at 12 months and we hold a unilateral exit. (4) Carve-outs exist: §6.2 preserves the Company's right to run its own closeout web site, the Deerskin Products definition excludes Joan Cook products, and §8(b) protects the existing Globix Agreement. Direction also favors us: the reciprocal covenant in §6.3 binds HDI on broader terms, with a two-year post-term tail that the Company does not bear, and the restriction is the consideration for HDI's exclusive-brand bargain. Nothing here approaches walk-away territory (no post-term non-compete and no undefined scope). Two minor sub-elements fall short of the preferred wording and are noted rather than flagged: there is no express carve-out for internal development or for businesses acquired by the Company, and "products substantially similar to Deerskin Products" is somewhat elastic. If this agreement is reopened for other reasons, we would add an acquisitions/internal-development carve-out to §6.2, but neither point is material enough to justify a redline on its own.

quote: 6.1 Except as provided in Section 6.2, during the term of this Agreement, the Company shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products (including, without limitation, the products of Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled and companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled) and HDI shall have the exclusive right to use of the "Deerskin" brand for a self-contained web site for the offering of Deerskin Products directly to the consumer on the Internet.
rationale: Section 6.1 binds the Company (our client) to exclusive dealing: it may not participate in any similar internet project for Deerskin Products or substantially similar products, and HDI holds the exclusive right to the "Deerskin" brand online. The restriction runs "during the term of this Agreement," and Section 4.1 makes the term automatically renew for successive one-year periods indefinitely unless terminated on 90 days' notice, with Section 4.2 imposing a Termination Payment if the Company terminates. There is no service-level regime and no termination-for-breach right; the only performance-based exit (Section 1.6) is a one-off right if the Site is not operational within 70 days of signature, which lapses at launch. The result is exclusive dealing for the full (potentially perpetual) term with no ongoing performance-based exit — walk-away territory under this rule, and short of the fallback's 12-month cap and automatic release on failure to meet service levels or delivery dates. Because HDI grants a reciprocal covenant in Section 6.3 (which benefits us and we leave intact), deleting the exclusivity outright would be disproportionate, so we redline to the fallback: a 12-month cap plus automatic termination of the restriction on any HDI delivery or performance failure. The product scope is tied to the defined term "Deerskin Products" and is acceptable; we note but do not separately flag the open-ended "companies similar to" wording.

The commercial terms are a fixed revenue share on Net Sales (Section 3.1), with no benchmarking or matching mechanic. rationale: The fee construct meets our preferred position: the Company owes HDI only a 30% revenue share on actual Net Sales above an $11,000 monthly threshold, so all amounts are purely usage/sales-based. The $11,000 figure is a floor below which nothing is payable (a benefit to us), not a minimum spend or take-or-pay obligation, and there is no shortfall, minimum volume or minimum-order language anywhere in the Agreement. Term is one year with automatic one-year renewals terminable by either Party on 90 days' notice (§4.1), plus an immediate termination right if the Site is not live in 70 days (§1.6), so we are never locked into a multi-year commitment. Noted but not flagged here: the §4.2 Termination Payment (half of trailing twelve-month Net Sales less $800,000) is an exit cost payable only if we terminate, and the §6.1 exclusivity restricts competing Deerskin web projects — both are termination/exclusivity issues for their own rules rather than minimum purchase commitments, and neither creates a purchase obligation. proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement has no limitation of liability, so both parties are exposed without limit and there is no exclusion of indirect damages. We have added a mutual cap at the greater of twelve (12) months' fees and USD 1,000,000, with indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement sitting outside the cap; we can accept a straight 12-month fee cap if the USD 1,000,000 floor is an issue.

ops.text: (c) Limitation of Liability. Except for Excluded Claims, (i) neither Party shall be liable to the other for any indirect, incidental, special, consequential or punitive damages, and (ii) each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (A) the fees paid or payable by the Company under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (B) One Million Dollars ($1,000,000). "Excluded Claims" means a Party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights. The Company's obligations to pay amounts due under Section 3 and Section 4.2 are not subject to the foregoing limitations.

proposal.summary: Insert a mutual liability cap with standard uncapped carve-outs into Section 9 (Warranties), which survives under Section 10.7.

rationale: The Agreement contains no limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages or aggregate-liability provision. Searches for "liability", "damages", "consequential" and "indemnif" return only the no-joint-venture language in Section 10.2 (p0061-p0062); the Warranties section (Sections 9(a)-(b)) is limited to authority representations and the Globix carve-out, and the Fees (Section 3) and Termination Payment (Section 4.2) provisions contain no cap. Both parties are therefore exposed to unlimited and consequential damages, which fails even the fallback (mutual 12-month fee cap with carve-outs for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct). We propose inserting a mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000, a mutual exclusion of indirect damages, and uncapped Excluded Claims, placed in Section 9 so that it survives under Section 10.7.

verification.notes: precision position: preferred fee limb uses the exact lowercase fee basis and claim anchor: Use the operative words 'fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim'; do not use defined capital-F Fees or an event anchor. precision position: Customer payment obligations are not damages: State that Customer's payment obligations, or all amounts due, are not damages; undisputed Fees for conforming Services is too narrow. The inserted clause is a concise, self-contained limitation of liability for a document that had none, and it leaves the existing Globix warranty paragraph untouched — minimality and intent are preserved. Two preferred elements fall short: the fee limb is anchored to 'the event giving rise to the claim' rather than the 12 months 'preceding the claim', and the payment-obligation sentence is drafted as a carve-out from the cap for amounts under Sections 3 and 4.2 rather than a statement that Customer's payment obligations are not 'damages' for cap purposes. Recommended fix without expanding the clause: replace 'immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim' with 'immediately preceding the claim', and replace the final sentence with 'The Company's obligations to pay amounts due under this Agreement are not "damages" for purposes of the foregoing limitations.' All required carve-outs, the mutual indirect-damages exclusion and the USD 1,000,000 limb are present, so the clause comfortably clears the fallback and sits above it; the shortfalls are wording-precision points to note in the rationale rather than material deviations.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement is silent on exit, yet HDI hosts the Site and holds our Content, user information and customer data. We have inserted a transition-assistance and data-return provision at our preferred position: up to six (6) months' assistance at HDI's then-current rates, return of our data within thirty (30) days in a standard machine-readable format, then deletion with written certification.

ops.text: 4.3 Transition Assistance; Return of Data. Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, HDI shall (a) at the Company's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for a period of up to six (6) months following the Termination Date at HDI's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days of the Termination Date, return to the Company all Content, user information and customer data of the Company then in HDI's possession or control, in a standard machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete all such Content, user information and customer data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing to the Company.

proposal.summary: Insert new Section 4.3 requiring HDI to provide up to six months' transition assistance at then-current rates and to return Company data within 30 days in a standard machine-readable format, then delete and certify deletion.

rationale: Section 4 (Term; Termination; Termination Payment) addresses only notice periods and the Termination Payment; there is no exit, transition-assistance, data-return, migration or deletion provision anywhere in the Agreement. This is a site development and hosting agreement in which HDI operates the Site on its own server (Sections 1.3, 1.4) and holds our Content, user information and customer data (Section 8.1), so on termination we would have no contractual right to recover that data or to obtain migration help. The confidentiality provisions (8.1-8.2) restrict use and disclosure but do not require return or deletion, and the survival clause (10.7) does not fill the gap. Playbook expects at minimum 90 days of transition assistance and data export within 30 days; nothing here meets even the fallback, so we insert a new Section 4.3 at the preferred position (up to six months' assistance at HDI's then-current rates, return within 30 days in machine-readable format, then certified deletion).

verification.notes: The Agreement was silent on exit; a single concise new Section 4.3 supplies all preferred elements: up-to-six-month assistance at then-current rates, 30-day return in standard machine-readable format, then deletion with written certification. The return deadline runs from the Termination Date, not from a Customer request; the "at the Company's request" condition attaches only to transition assistance and does not swallow the mandatory data-return, deletion or certification duties. No existing term was altered and no undefined term or dangling mechanic is introduced; "Termination Date" is an already-defined term and "Content, user information and customer data" tracks the hosting subject matter.
